source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ's LC8 campus in Ashburn publishes 756 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure for any Virginia facility.

The 756 MW sits against 850,000 square feet of technical space, about 889 watts per square foot. That density is well above a conventional enterprise data center and is the signature of power-dense compute. The operator publishes no rack count, so any rack or accelerator estimate requires an assumption the data does not supply.

Disclosure matters as much as size here. Only 29 of 376 mapped Virginia facilities publish a megawatt figure, and LC8 alone accounts for roughly 29 percent of the 2,563.4 MW those 29 facilities report. A single campus holding that share of published capacity reflects how little of the state's capacity is disclosed, not necessarily how much of it exists.

What the data does not cover: certifications, which would indicate what the campus is qualified to host, and any announced expansion. The 756 MW is a published specification, and the grid connection behind it determines when that capacity becomes usable.
